page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfc6.8xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 16 physical Intel Xeon 8269CY cores operating at a base frequency of 3.1 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture, this instance is configured with 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying instead on network-attached storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 10 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks place this instance in the middle tier for compute and memory operations. The Intel Xeon processor delivers a stress-ng single-core performance of 1435.39 and a multi-core score of 30631.79. The CPU supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and AVX512_VNNI, which accelerate vector calculations and deep learning inference. This is reflected in LLM inference benchmarks, where the instance processes 1563.07 tokens per second for a small 135M model and 46.11 tokens per second for a medium 7B model.

Memory performance is characterized by a read-only cached small block bandwidth of 1704.01 GB/sec, which drops to 104.96 GB/sec for uncached large blocks, alongside a write bandwidth of 36.58 GB/sec. In database operations, the instance achieves a PassMark database score of 11255.12 and handles 29.05 million Redis SET operations per second. These metrics indicate strong performance for transactional and in-memory workloads that fit within the 64.0 GB memory envelope.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.hfc6.8xlarge offers a high-density compute profile. By minimizing the memory-to-vCPU ratio and omitting bundled local storage or GPUs, it provides a cost-effective solution for CPU-bound workloads that do not require massive memory footprints. This makes the instance highly suitable for high-performance web serving, software compilation, batch processing, and medium-scale database hosting.
